newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rejects Bosnian Serb court ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rejects Bosnian Serb court ruling.

text.p: The United States on Monday rejected a ruling by the Bosnian Serb constitutional court that President Biljana Plavsic could not call early elections.
The ruling on Friday aggravated the political crisis in Bosnia, where Plavsic is in a power struggle with Serb hard-liners loyal to her predecessor, indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic.

The United States, which favors Plavsic's attempts to root out corruption in the Serb-ruled part of Bosnia, said last week the hard-liners were intimidating the court to rule against Plavsic's decision to dissolve the Serb parliament.
U.S. State Department spokesman James Rubin, in the first official U.S. comment since the court made its ruling, said on Monday: "We reject the decision of the court.

"Her (Plavsic's) action was clearly legal and ... the constitutional court was subjected to intimidation and politicization." The spokesman cited the beating in a police station of Jovo Rosic, one of the judges in the court.

"The attack on a judge who was involved in the court ruling ... (is) outrageous. There are still some people in this part of the world who haven't got it yet -- that as long as they continue to pursue these tactics, they and the people they claim to represent are going to suffer," Rubin added.

In the Bosnian town of Banja Luka, Plavsic also dismissed the court ruling and said she would keep working to hold the elections on Oct. 12. "I say they (the court rulings) are not binding for me," she added.

Rubin said: "Mrs. Plavsic, the elected president of the Bosnian Serb Republic, is making clear that she's on the side of those who want Dayton (the Dayton peace agreement) implemented. She's on the side of those who want prosperity and a return to Europe for their people."
